title: Two Indians among 11 hurt in drone strike on Riyadh business tower; India condemns attack
dek: Saudi authorities blamed Yemen's Houthis for the second strike on the capital's business district in under a week. The MEA said the Indian embassy is helping the injured.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Two Indian nationals were among 11 people injured when a drone struck a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District on Tuesday, Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said, in the second attack on the Saudi capital's business district in less than a week. India's Ministry of External Affairs condemned the attack on Wednesday and said its embassy was helping the injured and their families.

Saudi Civil Defence, which described the attack as a terrorist act by Yemen's Houthi movement, said the injured were two Saudi citizens, two Indian residents, three Nepalese residents and four Egyptians. It did not say how badly they were hurt. Emergency teams reached the site quickly, it said.

## What happened

The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen did not name the building. Three witnesses said the drone hit the headquarters of the Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund and the country's tallest skyscraper, according to reports. A photograph released by Civil Defence showed damage roughly halfway up the facade.

The coalition's spokesman, Major General Turki al-Maliki, called it a "cowardly terrorist attack" and said investigators were at the site. He said the deliberate targeting of civilians would meet a firm response.

Unlike in recent attacks, no emergency alert was sent to mobile phones before the strike, according to reports; one witness said a vehicle with a loudspeaker warned pedestrians to take cover. Saudi Public Security has warned residents against filming or sharing information about interceptions or impact sites, and the Indian embassy in Riyadh urged the Indian community to follow local rules.

No Houthi statement on Tuesday's strike had been reported by Wednesday afternoon India time. On Monday, the Houthi-run communications ministry said coalition airstrikes in Yemen's Hodeidah governorate had hit telecommunications buildings, workers' housing and a mosque, killing 17 workers and injuring 11 in an initial count. That account could not be independently confirmed.

## India's response

"We strongly condemn the attack on one of the towers of the financial district in Riyadh on November 24 as well as the continued attacks targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," the ministry said. It said such attacks endangered civilian lives, violated Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and undermined regional security, called for their "immediate cessation", and expressed solidarity with the Saudi government and people.

Saudi Arabia is home to one of the largest Indian communities abroad, and the Gulf as a whole is a leading source of remittances to India, which makes the widening war a direct concern for Indian families as well as for New Delhi's energy supplies. Qatar, the UAE, Kuwait, Lebanon, Pakistan and the United States also condemned the attack, and the secretary-general of the Gulf Cooperation Council called it "a heinous crime", according to reports.

## Background

On 19 November a Houthi strike damaged several floors of a tower in the same district and neighbouring buildings, with no injuries reported. Fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, largely paused under a 2022 truce, resumed in July alongside the wider US-Iran conflict. The Houthis, who control Sanaa and much of western Yemen, have since fired missiles and drones at Saudi airports, oil facilities and office buildings, while the coalition has carried out widespread airstrikes in Yemen.

The deadliest attack came on 10 October, when a missile hit a passenger terminal at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. Saudi aviation authorities said 12 people were killed; later reports put the toll at 13.

## What happens next

The coalition has promised a response, and its pattern in recent weeks has been to follow major attacks on Saudi cities with strikes on Houthi missile and drone sites in Yemen. Most international flights to Riyadh have been cancelled and major events, including AFC Asian Cup matches, postponed or cancelled, according to reports.
